title.value: Explaining Black Boxes on Sequential Data Using Weighted Automata
title.justification: The title establishes a focus on using weighted automata to interpret the behavior of black-box models on sequential data, aligning with the paper's key theme of extracting weighted finite automata from models like RNNs.
title.quote: In the case of sequential data, particular attention has been given to the problem of extracting, from a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), a weighted finite automaton (WFA).

analysis.description: This paper explores the problem of approximate minimization for language models, aiming to replace a black-box model with a weighted finite automaton (WFA) that maintains the original model's functionality while adhering to size constraints and minimizing approximation errors. It applies Hankel matrix concepts and AAK theory to handle black boxes trained over sequential data with a one-letter alphabet, presenting a novel algorithm for WFA extraction.

type.justification: The paper is focused on presenting theoretical approaches, algorithms, and proofs to address the approximate minimization problem using concepts from control theory, AAK theory, and spectral norms.
type.quote: This means that addressing the approximate minimization problem using the spectral norm can facilitate the comparison between different classes of models, and the development of a distance that can be precisely computed and minimized.

name.justification: The paper develops methods for extracting and approximating models used in language modelling, specifically focusing on sequences over a one-letter alphabet.
name.quote: We present a new theoretical framework for WFA extraction from a black box trained for language modelling of sequential data over a one-letter alphabet.

name.justification: The paper discusses extracting WFAs specifically from Recurrent Neural Networks, highlighting their relationship and comparative efficiency.
name.quote: It is possible because Hankel matrices are at the core of the influential work of Adamyan et al., which constitutes the main theoretical background on which we build our analysis. This theory has been applied before to the approximate minimization problem for WFAs, but the approach relies on the Hankel matrix considered to have known finite rank, so it cannot be directly generalized [Balle et al., 2021].

name.justification: The primary model extracted and discussed in the paper is the Weighted Finite Automaton (WFA), which it aims to derive from other models like RNNs.
name.quote: In fact, WFAs are a less expensive alternative to RNNs, while still being expressive and suited for sequence modelling and prediction.

name.justification: The paper frequently references using RNNs as the original model from which a WFA is extracted for approximate minimization.
name.quote: In the case of sequential data, particular attention has been given to the problem of extracting, from a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), a weighted finite automaton (WFA).

is_contributed.justification: The Recurrent Neural Network is not introduced by the paper; rather, it is used as a base model for extraction of the WFA.
is_contributed.quote: In the case of sequential data, particular attention has been given to the problem of extracting, from a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), a weighted finite automaton (WFA).

is_executed.justification: The paper does not conduct experiments or execution tests of RNNs; it primarily focuses on theoretical derivation and extraction.
is_executed.quote: The task of knowledge distillation is closely related to the more general approximate minimization problem, where the objective is to find a model, smaller than the original one, that imitates its behaviour while minimizing the approximation error.

is_compared.justification: RNNs are used as a reference model for extraction but not compared in a numerical scheme in the paper.
is_compared.quote: We present a new theoretical framework for WFA extraction from a black box trained for language modelling of sequential data over a one-letter alphabet.

referenced_paper_title.justification: The foundational paper for RNNs is referenced concerning their use for sequence modelling, underscoring the importance of Hochreiter and Schmidhuber's work in the context of this paper.

name.justification: WFAs are the focal models in this paper as the method aims to derive them as computationally efficient alternatives to sequence models like RNNs.
name.quote: and we prove that our method returns an asymptotically-optimal approximation.

is_contributed.justification: The concept of WFAs is not novel in this paper; it applies existing knowledge of WFAs to approximate minimization.
is_contributed.quote: In the case of sequential data, particular attention has been given to the problem of extracting, from a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), a weighted finite automaton (WFA).

is_executed.justification: The paper does not include execution experiments with WFAs but theoretically derives and discusses their extraction.
is_executed.quote: The task of knowledge distillation is closely related to the more general approximate minimization problem, where the objective is to find a model, smaller than the original one, that imitates its behaviour while minimizing the approximation error.

is_compared.justification: WFAs are not directly compared against other models numerically in this paper, as the focus is more on extraction and approximation.
is_compared.quote: We do not assume any knowledge on the internal structure of the black box, nor on the training data.

referenced_paper_title.value: Optimal Spectral-Norm Approximate Minimization of Weighted Finite Automata
referenced_paper_title.justification: This paper by Balle et al. is referenced for using AAK theory for spectral-norm minimization of WFAs.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Balle et al. [2021] use AAK theory to address the optimal spectral-norm approximate minimization problem for a large class of WFAs over a one-letter alphabet.
